title: The Babysitter's Third Rule
concept: Rules on the fridge for a babysitter: 1. Bedtime is 8. 2. No sugar. 3. If he asks to be let out of his room, he is already in bed.
setting: Family kitchen, upstairs landing, a locked child's room.
conflict: A small voice behind the door begs to be let out; Sam is also asleep in his bed.
escalation: Both 'Sams' start asking Priya which one is real.
reveal: The parents' rules were never about the one in the room — the one in the bed is the one they're afraid of.
ending: Priya opens the bedroom door to check. The bed is empty. The voice behind the locked door goes silent and says 'thank you.'

hooks.line: Rule 3 on the fridge said: if he asks to be let out, he's already in bed.
hooks.first_visual: A fridge note held by a magnet.

hooks.line: The boy I'm babysitting is asleep in his bed. He's also knocking on his door.
Only one of them could be real. I had to open one door.
'Priya, it's me. Let me out. The other one isn't me.'
Which one would you let out?

originality_review: Babysitter-in-peril is a classic set-up; the two-children rule twist is original. Watch similarity against existing 'rules' channels.
